IBM.rationale: IBM presents a compelling value-at-floor-of-range setup with improving fundamentals. Pillar 1 (fundamentals): Q1 2026 showed strong YoY improvement — revenue +9.5%, EPS +14.3%, net income +15.3%, operating cash flow +18.3% — with gross margin expanding to 56.2% from 55.2%. Software ARR reached $24.6B (+$3B YoY), $69B RPO provides multi-year visibility, and segment profit grew +21.3% YoY. The franchise is defensible: Red Hat OpenShift, watsonx ($5B+ book), IBM Z handling 70% of global transactional workflows, and HashiCorp adding hybrid-cloud capabilities. However, consulting is soft (+0.9% cc), federal contract cancellations ($100M) create headwinds, and the balance sheet carries elevated leverage (liabilities/equity 3.73x, long-term debt $57.7B post-Confluent). Pillar 2 (valuation): PE at 19.3x is at the absolute floor of its 365-day range (19.0–51.2), having compressed 60%+ from 46x a year ago while fundamentals improved. P/B at 6.29x is also at floor (6.2–10.8). Earnings yield of 5.2% exceeds the 10Y Treasury (4.47%) by 73bps. The advisory note that adjusted EPS of $1.91 implies a PE of ~12.5x makes the valuation case even more compelling, though I anchor to the GAAP figure for conservatism. Pillar 3 (catalyst): The dividend increase to $1.69/quarter (~3.1% yield) signals management confidence in FCF durability; FedRAMP expansion of 11 AI/automation products opens a regulated federal route-to-market; and the Confluent integration provides a data-streaming capability that deepens the platform. These are dated, fundamental catalysts. The principal risks — high leverage in a rising-rate environment, consulting softness, and quarterly earnings volatility — cap the score below +0.5. The verification note that the price decline decelerated (not accelerated as the quant report stated) is a minor narrative correction but does not change the fundamental picture.
